features.description: Unified render gate: a single deterministic function every ActionItem passes through before it can render, returning exactly one of three total, mutually-exclusive outcomes — render (Needs Action), suppress (not relevant or resolved), or demote (cannot prove → uncertainty). It is the ONLY decision point and the ONLY demotion path; F004 owns constructing the demotion card but never decides demotion independently. The gate order is normative: (1) scope applies to selected scope? else SUPPRESS (not relevant to this view); (2) source fresh AND evaluable? else DEMOTE; (3) clears_when present AND evaluable? else DEMOTE; (4) resolution_class set? else DEMOTE; (5) predicate resolved? SUPPRESS; (6) else (unresolved) RENDER. This inverts suppress_resolved's default from render-unless-proven-resolved to suppress-unless-proven-live. Reuses 001's closed predicate registry; adds no DSL.
steps: Define render_decision(card, *, selected_scope, live_state, now) -> Literal['render','suppress','demote'] in a render_gate module, implementing the six-step normative order exactly
Wire dashboard._gather_action_items to route every card through render_decision; the rendered Needs Action set is exactly the cards returning 'render'
Preserve 001's suppress audit trail; add a demote audit trail (which step triggered demotion)

Tests: a truth/decision table covering each of the six steps in order, including ties (scope fails AND stale -> suppress wins because scope is checked first); the three outcomes are total and mutually exclusive; this is the only function that returns 'demote'
features.acceptance: render_decision is a single function implementing the six-step normative order (scope→fresh→clears_when→resolution_class→resolved→render) and is the only path producing render/suppress/demote. The rendered Needs Action set equals exactly the cards returning 'render'. A decision table test exercises each step (including precedence ties: scope-fail short-circuits to suppress before staleness is checked) and proves the outcomes are total and mutually exclusive. No other module returns a demote decision.

features.description: Explicit producer-asserted scope, no silent inference. Add scope (global|fleet|project|plan|feature) plus optional plan_id/feature_id to ActionItem; NEW producers MUST set scope explicitly (no constructor default that infers scope from project_name — that would quietly recreate the heuristic problem and make legacy cards look trustworthy). Legacy/unscoped items (scope unset) route through an explicit legacy_adapter path that logs a deprecation warning and is eligible for demotion; they are never silently treated as belonging to the selected project. A scope-applicability lattice drives render: global applies to every project/fleet view; fleet applies to the fleet view; project applies only to its own project; plan/feature scope applies ONLY IF its plan_id resolves to the selected project — if resolution fails, the gate demotes (does not render).
steps: Add scope (enum, required for new producers) + optional plan_id/feature_id to operator_console.ActionItem; do NOT add a project_name-inferring default

Set scope explicitly in every producer: reconcile/install/global-capability -> global; per-project gates/architecture/build-warnings -> project (+project_name); plan-gate -> plan (+plan_id); feature-gate -> feature (+plan_id/feature_id)

Implement scope_applies(card, *, selected_scope, selected_project, resolve_plan_to_project) lattice; plan/feature requires resolve_plan_to_project(card.plan_id) == selected_project, else the lattice returns 'unresolved' and the gate demotes
Route scope-unset legacy items through legacy_adapter that logs a deprecation warning; remove reliance on is_item_relevant_to_project as the primary path (keep it only behind legacy_adapter)

Tests: lattice truth table (global->project view applies; project A card->project B view not-applies; fleet->project not-applies; plan card whose plan_id resolves to selected project applies; plan card that fails resolution demotes); a test proving NO silent project_name inference (an unscoped card does not render as project work — it logs + is demotion-eligible)
features.acceptance: Every producer emits cards with an explicit scope; there is no constructor default that infers scope from project_name. scope_applies implements the documented lattice including plan/feature → project resolution (failed resolution yields demote, not render). Scope-unset legacy items pass through a logged legacy_adapter and are demotion-eligible, never silently rendered as project work. Verified by a lattice truth-table test (incl. plan-resolution success and failure) and a no-silent-inference test.

features.description: Per-source freshness: extend freshness from 004's snapshot-wide envelope to per-source/per-card stamping. Each card resolves the source it was computed from, when that source last evaluated successfully, and whether that evaluation succeeded — so one stale or failed producer demotes only its own cards without poisoning fresh siblings. Feeds F001 step 2 (source fresh AND evaluable?) and F004 (demotion).
steps: Populate source_evaluated_at + source_eval_ok per source when each producer runs (a source-freshness map keyed by source id, or fields on the card)
Compute per-source is_stale against DASHBOARD_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_SECONDS using the source's OWN evaluated_at, not the snapshot generated_at
Expose source_freshness(card, *, now) -> {evaluated_at, age, is_stale, eval_ok} for gate + demotion use

Tests: a card from a stale source reports is_stale while a sibling from a fresh source does not, in the same snapshot; eval_ok=False (recompute failed/skipped) is reported distinctly from is_stale (old-but-evaluated)
features.acceptance: Each card resolves a per-source freshness ({evaluated_at, age, is_stale, eval_ok}) from its own source's last evaluation, independent of the snapshot-wide envelope. In one snapshot, a stale-source card is is_stale while a fresh-source sibling is not; eval_ok=False is distinct from is_stale. Verified by mixed-freshness-source tests.

features.description: Generalize stale/failed-to-uncertainty demotion to ALL producers, with an explicit band/section. When the render gate (F001) returns 'demote' for a card because its source is stale or eval_ok is False, that source's cards are replaced by exactly one demotion card: title 'Status could not be refreshed: <source>', detail naming last-checked time + reason, with band=Band.INFO (priority 2, below ADVISORY), resolution_class=blocked_external, and section='status_uncertain' (a dedicated lower-priority section). N cards from one stale source collapse to one uncertainty card; zero of them render as Needs Action. This lifts the architecture-only pattern (004 F007 render_architecture_status) into the shared demotion-card builder so reconcile, capabilities, gates, and architecture all demote identically. F004 builds the card; F001 owns the demote DECISION (no second decision path).
steps: Add a build_uncertainty_card(source, *, last_checked, reason) -> ActionItem helper: band=Band.INFO, resolution_class=blocked_external (or RESOLUTION_BLOCKED_EXTERNAL), section='status_uncertain'
In the render pipeline, collapse all 'demote'-decided cards sharing a source into one uncertainty card per source
Route architecture's existing demotion through build_uncertainty_card (architecture becomes one caller, not a special case); keep render_architecture_status behavior as a thin adapter

Tests: a stale reconcile source yields exactly one status_uncertain INFO card and zero reconcile Needs Action cards; capabilities and gates demote identically; the uncertainty card states source + last-checked + reason; architecture parity preserved
features.acceptance: For any source the gate demotes (stale or eval_ok False), its cards are replaced by exactly one uncertainty card with band=Band.INFO, resolution_class=blocked_external, section='status_uncertain', stating source + last-checked + reason, and zero of its cards appear as Needs Action. Reconcile, capabilities, gates, and architecture demote through the same build_uncertainty_card path. Verified by per-producer staleness tests including architecture parity.

features.description: Global/project separation plus the four-part render-truth invariant, with the QuantRE regression pinned. A global producer emits exactly one scope=global card; a project view shows it with a GLOBAL badge iff its live predicate is unresolved AND its source fresh, hides it when the live global predicate is clean, and NEVER resurrects a now-clean global card from a per-project output cache (what-now-cache.json) — the gate re-evaluates the global predicate against live global state, not cache contents. An invariant test asserts that for any selected scope S, every visible Needs Action card satisfies all four: scope_applies(card.scope,S) AND per-source-fresh AND clears_when unresolved-and-evaluable AND resolution_class set. The QuantRE regression is an explicit acceptance case. Depends on F001, F002, F003, F004.
steps: Render a GLOBAL badge for scope=global cards shown in a non-global view; suppress the global card when its live predicate evaluates clean
Re-evaluate the global predicate against live global state at render time; ensure a per-project output cache cannot re-surface a global card whose predicate is now resolved
Add a render_truth_invariant(rendered_needs_action, *, selected_scope, live_state, now) assertion (test helper, optionally a build-time check) over the rendered Needs Action set

QuantRE regression fixture: selected project = quantre-migration, a stale per-project reconcile cache saying missing_snapshot, and a clean live global reconcile check -> assert zero setup-drift Needs Action cards rendered

Tests: a global reconcile issue shows with GLOBAL badge while unresolved+fresh, disappears when global reconcile is clean, is not resurrected from a stale per-project cache; the four-part invariant holds over a mixed global/project/stale/resolved fixture
features.acceptance: Global-scoped cards render in project views only with a GLOBAL badge and only while their live predicate is unresolved and source fresh; they vanish when the live global predicate is clean and are never resurrected from a per-project cache (predicate re-evaluated live, not read from cache). The QuantRE regression — selected project=quantre-migration + stale per-project missing_snapshot cache + clean live global reconcile — renders zero setup-drift Needs Action cards, proven by a committed fixture. An invariant test proves that for the selected scope, every visible Needs Action card satisfies scope ∧ per-source-fresh ∧ unresolved ∧ resolution_class, over a mixed global/project/stale/resolved fixture. Full orchestrate sweep stays green.
